A cat takes its row, column and coloured: A cat blocks the rest of its row, its column and its colour region. It also blocks nearby squares where another cat would touch it. A placement can narrow the options in a region that looks unrelated at first.
A legal claim can still leave an awkward: Before making a claim, identify which tiles it uses and what will remain. This helps you avoid accepting a set you did not mean to make.
A mixed office releases both colours wit: A building marked 6 + 3 sends two groups together. If only the smaller group has a bus, three will board and six may keep circling. Reserve space for those six.
A question mark hides a rear office’s pa: A question mark hides the workers in a rear building. Open the office ahead of it to bring it forward. Once the faces appear, compare them with your four active buses before tapping again.
A rider boards automatically when passin: A rider boards as they pass a matching stop. Wait without spending a turn, or use 2× to speed up. Once every office is empty and the last falling worker has entered the loop, the whole game automatically runs at 4× until the final pickup. Keys 1–5 open offices from left to right.
A temporary slot holds a screw until a b: A temporary slot holds a screw whose colour has no available matching box. It is a small amount of working space, not another colour collection. When a suitable box opens, waiting screws move into it automatically.
After each tap, watch the pickup counter: Open one matching office and wait for its nine workers to board before choosing the next. After three releases, 27 workers have boarded. Clear all six offices to board all 54 and finish the level.
After the second blue box closes, both o: The picture shows why “keep taking blue” is not a rule for the whole board. A blue screw that fitted a moment ago would now need a temporary slot. The current boxes decide which colours you can collect directly.
Aim coloured balls into matching groups: Shoot coloured balls in Pool Shoot Tournament. Aim for connected groups and use rebounds when the front row blocks your shot.
An arrow moves headfirst and needs a cle: An arrow slides in the direction it points and needs a clear lane all the way out. A gap immediately in front of it can be misleading. A blocker farther down the same lane makes the move unsafe.
An available jump takes priority over a: At the start of a turn, look for captures first. A jump can be compulsory, so check the board before deciding which piece to advance. If several captures are open, think about where each piece will finish and what your opponent can jump in reply.
An open tile has nothing on top of it an: Look at the stack before looking for symbols. A tile needs to be uncovered and have a free side. A matching mark on a buried tile gives you a goal for a later move, but only the pieces that are free can leave.
Arrange characters and props in Sprunki: Set up a physics scene in Sprunki Sandbox: Ragdoll Playground Mode. Place characters and props, then test how they fall and collide.
Assemble a jigsaw online in Favorite Puz: Build a picture in Favorite Puzzles, an online jigsaw game. Pick a piece count, start from the edges and try rotation for a harder puzzle.
At 27/27, give a matching rider time to: If someone on the loop can board, or a full bus is departing, give it time. A jam occurs when all places are occupied, a rider is waiting to enter, and no current pickup or departure can help.
Before lifting a screw, check which hole: The empty holes are your working space. Before lifting a screw, see whether moving it will take a plate off the board or leave you with the same plate and one less usable hole. The best move often opens a hole you could not use earlier.
Before opening another office, count how: Read the first bus in each of the four queues before releasing an office. Say red is behind blue in one lane. Riders who need red will keep circling until three blue riders fill that front bus and send it away. Check whether you have room for that wait before you let another group out.
Both of your players jump together. Watc: Your players move together on a jump. Watch the ball and their lean before pressing the key. An early jump can put you in the air too soon, leaving the ball free by the time you land.
Both players in a duel use the same keyb: In a duel, both players use the same keyboard. Leave space for each person's hand, then test movement and jumping before racing. In solo practice you can slow down at a corner and see where you need to land.
Build a room and dress a character in TB: Create rooms and characters in TB World. Arrange furniture, pick outfits and use the props to set up a scene of your own.
Build four foundations from Ace through: The four foundations grow from Ace to King in suit order. To reach the cards you need, rearrange the columns on the board. When you have a choice, move a card that uncovers a face-down one. The new card can give you a move the visible board is missing.
Build towers along the road in Epic Empi: Defend a fantasy kingdom in Epic Empire: Tower Defense. Place towers along the road and use hero abilities where enemy waves break through.
Buy and plant eggs in Grow Slime, then c: Raise slimes from eggs in Grow Slime. Learn how to plant eggs, leave room to reach them and collect the slimes that hatch.
Change size with Q and E to get through: Change your size to clear jumps and tight spaces in Your Obby Size. Learn the Q and E controls and plan where you will land.
Check a strand’s colour against the boxe: Read the shape and the sorting boxes together. A strand may be easy to pull, but if its box is closed you need a slot to hold it. Look for something you can send straight to an open box first.
Check beneath a plate before removing it: Removing a last screw can expose several colours. Check which boxes are open before releasing the plate.
Check the board after a plate moves. It: Glass swings around its last screw. Empty glass falls, or rests on another plate until its support moves. Other exposed screws remain playable during movement. Pack every screw, including those in the tray, to win.
Check the colours on top of the stacks a: The hexagon shape lets one stack touch several neighbours. Look at the colours on the nearby stacks before you use an empty cell. A good placement gives the colour you want to collect somewhere to go.
Check the loaded ball before aiming at a: This table plays like an arcade colour shooter. The ball you have loaded tells you which group to aim at. Look closely at the edge of a cluster. A shot that clips a different ball on the way can miss the match entirely.
Check the size you need at the far end o: Before you resize, look at the whole obstacle. A low opening may call for a smaller character. Once you get through, check the landing space and the next jump before changing back.
Check what changed after your opponent’s: Before choosing an attack, look at the last piece your opponent moved and what it can now reach. If one of your pieces can be taken, check whether it is defended and what you could take back.
Choose a dish, shop for its ingredients: Shop for ingredients, prepare a dish and serve it on a livestream in ASMR Girl: Livestream Mukbang.
Choose a game and difficulty in Solitair: Choose a variant and difficulty in Solitaire The Collection. Read what a completed deal looks like before moving cards out of their starting piles.
Choose a number from the palette and fil: Choose a number from the palette and find the matching squares in the picture. Broad patches are easy to see. After those are filled, work around the edge of each patch for the lone squares that break up the outline.
Choose a palette number and work through: A solid patch of the same number goes quickly. Select it in the palette and work across the patch a row at a time. If you see a different number inside it, leave that square for its own colour.
Choose a treatment in Ellie Summer Spa &: Follow Ellie's summer spa routine. Choose a treatment, use the highlighted tools and complete the on-screen steps in order.
Choose a vehicle and place the ramp or o: The decisions happen before you press Start. Pick a vehicle and place an obstacle where it can affect the run. Give the setup a first attempt, then look at where the figure left the vehicle and what it hit.
Choose an animal and give it a hairstyle: Give animals new hairstyles in Animal Hair Salon. Pick a pet, try the tools along the bottom and choose accessories after styling.
Choose Klondike, Spider, FreeCell or Pyr: Play Klondike, Spider, FreeCell or Pyramid in one Solitaire collection. Choose a layout and learn what counts as a match in each mode.
Choose one digit missing from the box. C: List its missing digits. For each one, cross off the blank cells where the row or column already contains it.
Choose one of the 13 caves. Use the left: Choose a level. Use left click, Space or a touch input to steer the arrow.
Choose the hair and main outfit for each: Pick a hairstyle and outfit for each character first and see how their shapes look together. To tie the pair together, repeat one colour in the other person's shoes or accessories. You can leave the two outfits different and still make them look like a pair.
Choose the kind of deal you want to solv: Pick a variant by the sort of board you want to solve. Some deals give you four suit piles to build. Others ask you to clear a pattern or arrange descending sequences. Look at the rules of the selected variant before sending a card to a pile.
Clear a layered board in Mahjong Classic: Play Mahjong Classic solitaire and clear a layered board. Learn which tiles are open, how flower pairs work and what to uncover first.
Clear every arrow from the grid without: Clear the grid in Arrow Exit Puzzle without running out of hearts. Check each arrow's full exit lane before tapping it.
Clear full rows and columns in Block Bla: Fit blocks into a grid and clear full lines in Block Blast Master. Check all three shapes before you place one and leave room for the next batch.
Clear the board before the shot counter: Clear Bubble Pop Legend levels before your shots run out. Use the next bubble and the move counter to plan two shots at a time.
Clock Out! is a bus sorting puzzle about: It is the end of the shift, and nine coworkers come out of each office together. A shuttle takes three riders of its own colour. Three buses can take a single-colour group home, provided the right colour is at the front when the riders arrive.
Clock Out! Level 1 Walkthrough | tapmelo: Level 1: plan the first departure | tapmelo
Clock Out! Mixed and Question-Mark Offic: Mystery offices and mixed shifts | tapmelo
Clock Out! Waiting Loop and Bus Jams | t: Room for the next shift | tapmelo
Collect smaller cubes along a route that: Pick up smaller cubes along a route that gives you a way out. If a large snake is coming across the path, turn before you get close enough to be forced into a corner.
Colour pixel art by number. Drag across: Make pixel art in Coloring Book: Color By Number. Drag across matching squares to colour large patches, then check the corners for gaps.
Compare Seven Pairs, Thirteen Orphans, A: After four sets and a pair, look at seven pairs, thirteen orphans and a few common patterns. Focus on how the tiles fit before worrying about scores.
Complete quests in Bubble Blast by firin: Pop bubble clusters and finish quests in Bubble Blast. Read the board objective and save bonuses for a group you cannot reach.
Count the turns before you select the pa: Picture the route as one, two or three straight segments. If any segment runs through a tile, choose another pair.
Create a family in Minni Family Home and: Make a family in Minni Family Home, visit places around Town and use the objects in each room to act out a scene.
Defend the lanes in Plants vs Zombies Hy: Defend the lanes in Plants vs Zombies Hybrids. Balance ordinary plants, stronger hybrids and cooldowns before the next zombie wave.
Deploy tank warriors from different eras: Deploy tank warriors across different eras. Read the front line and choose when to spend your resources in Age of Tanks Warriors: TD War.
Drag characters into empty slots to make: Make a loop in Sprunki by adding character sounds. Start with a beat, layer another sound and listen to the loop before filling every slot.
Drag one sound into an empty slot and li: Put a steady sound in an open slot and listen until the loop comes back around. Add a second part where there is room in the beat. You can hear how two characters interact before bringing more sounds into the mix.
Drag two identical items together to mak: Emily's café is tied to a merge board. Drag two identical items together to make the next ingredient or dish in that chain. The orders tell you what needs to come out of the kitchen. Work on the café and mansion between batches.
Draw a barrier between the dog and the b: Draw a wall to protect the dog from bees in Save The Pets. Keep both ends covered and hold out until the timer expires.
Drop matching fruit into the container a: Drop matching fruit and work toward a watermelon in Fruit Merge: Juicy Drop Game. Keep the pile low so there is room for your next drop.
Drop two identical fruits so they touch: Two identical fruits merge when they touch, making the next fruit in the chain. Drop each new fruit from above and let the pile settle. A fruit can roll down the side of a bigger one, so the point where you release it and the point where it lands may be different.
Each of the 13 caves has Arrow and Wheel: Read the next opening before the arrow gets there. If the passage narrows near the top, correct your direction while there is still space below. Waiting until you are beside a wall can leave too little room to turn.
Each row, column and 3×3 box must contai: A classic Sudoku uses digits 1 through 9 once in each row, each column and each 3×3 box. The clues already on the board are fixed. Use the clues to rule out places a digit cannot go.
Earn an extra bolt from a chest or the r: Use an extra bolt once you have earned one from the game's rewards. It gives you another place to sort or park nuts.
Every shot uses one move. A group pops o: Bubble Pop Legend gives you a limited number of shots on each board. Three or more joined bubbles of one colour pop. A well-placed shot through a narrow gap can clear the attachment holding up a much larger part of the board.
Explore The Aesthetic World of Obby and: Explore The Aesthetic World of Obby. Set your camera for platform jumps, control the run-up and find the character customisation menu.
Fill a pixel picture by matching the num: Colour a pixel picture by number in Color Pixels. Work through one palette number and find the single squares hidden along the outline.
Find a front-row office that matches a s: Start with a front office whose colour appears at the head of a bus queue. Tap the office or press 1–5 on a keyboard to release its nine riders.
Find a front-row office whose riders mat: Choose one of the five front buildings. All nine workers inside head down the ramp. Their colours and faces tell you which shuttles they can board.
Find frogs tucked into black-and-white d: Find frogs in black-and-white scenes. Look for eyes, bent legs and other frog outlines hidden among the drawing's lines.
Find hidden objects among the furniture: Search hotel rooms for hidden objects in My Hotel. Check the list, pan past the furniture and zoom into small details.
Find hidden words in a letter grid. Trac: Find words hidden across a letter grid. Check rows, columns and diagonals, and use unusual letter pairs to spot the longest words.
Find the first six blue screws and the n: Try the glass garden: opening moves, temporary slots and the choices that can jam your round.
Fire a bubble into a group of the same c: You fire one coloured bubble at a time. A shot pops bubbles when it joins enough of the same colour to make a group of at least three. A match near the ceiling can also drop bubbles hanging from it, which makes the position of a group as useful as its size.
Five Mahjong Waits and Their Winning Til: Five common waits: find every winning tile

Fly the Arrow and steer the Wheel throug: Steer an arrow to the portal in Geometry Arrow 2. Use Space, a mouse click or touch and practise short inputs for narrow cave gaps.
Follow a long arrow from its tip to the: Pick a long arrow near the middle and follow the space in front of its tip. The first arrow in its way gives you something concrete to solve. If that arrow is blocked too, follow its direction until you reach a piece that can leave.
Follow a six-move opening for Clock Out!: Send 54 animals home in six moves. The first level teaches the basics with three colours.
Follow the direction a wooden block need: The face you see first tells you only part of the story. Follow the direction a piece needs to slide. A long block can have a clear end on one face and run into a second piece hidden just around the corner.
From here, choose moves based on the ope: These moves explain the opening; they are not a complete click-by-click solution. Later choices depend on what you have already removed. After a plate swings or falls, scan the whole board for a useful exposed match instead of staying in one corner.
Give the loop time if a rider can still: Watch the buses for a moment. If a rider can still board or a full shuttle is pulling away, a space can open. A jam happens when a rider is waiting to enter and neither boarding nor a bus change can make room.
Give the room a purpose before filling i: Start with one thing happening in the room. For a character coming home, put the important objects by the entrance and leave a clear space for the character. A few useful items can give the scene a purpose before you add more furniture.
Give yourself a fixed point in each scen: Pick a doorway, a shop window or an edge of the scene as a landmark before you start panning. Search up and down one strip, move to the next, and use the landmark to remember where you stopped.
Glass Twist is a screw puzzle with movin: In Glass Twist, every pull changes the shape of the board. A plate can swing on its last screw, drop onto another plate or uncover several screws at once. Look at what the glass is holding up before you remove a fastener.
Glass Twist Level 2 Walkthrough: Glass G: Glass Twist level 2: the glass garden
Glass Twist Level 2 Guide: Opening Moves & Slot Strategy | tapmelo
Goblins, ogres and bosses follow the roa: Goblins, ogres and bosses come down the road in waves. Towers do the steady work while heroes can respond to trouble further along the route. Look for a bend near the start. A tower that covers the road on both sides of the bend gets longer to hit enemies.
Grow your cube snake by collecting small: Grow a cube snake in Snake 2048. Steer toward smaller cubes and leave enough space to turn away from larger snakes.
Guide an arrow through narrow passages i: Guide an arrow along musical obstacle courses in Geometry: Black Wave. Pick a difficulty and learn where small inputs help in narrow gaps.
Hold to draw the bow in Archery Ragdoll: Draw and release a bow in Archery Ragdoll. Time your shot as the archer sways and correct your aim after a miss.
How the glass and sorting boxes work: Sorting screws without filling the tray
How to Organise a Mahjong Hand: Organising a hand: finding the groups

If a green bus has two riders and a blue: An almost-full bus is one rider away from uncovering its next colour. If several workers need that next colour, finishing this particular bus can free more room than boarding one rider in a different lane.
If another plate overlaps the head, move: Seeing a screw does not mean it is exposed. A covered screw cannot be removed; a partially covered one may bounce back. Work on the covering plate and try the screw again once its head is clear.
If space is tight, check the next office: If the loop is getting crowded, wait for boarding to finish. Open the next office when you know where its first riders will go.
If two vehicles can leave the lot, start: When choosing between two vehicles, favour the one that can fill up and leave. Then reread the queue.
In later levels, an office can send more: Every level begins with accessible bus colours and a short easy section. Next come partial pickups and queue changes; blocked targets and mixed offices are saved for the later stages. From level 2, late mixed bottlenecks can leave only three free places, so keep room for the target colour.
In the beginner and intermediate exercis: When someone declares a win, look at how the tiles fit together. Beginner and intermediate exercises use one structure: four sets and a pair. Seven pairs and thirteen orphans come later in the advanced lessons.
In waiting-hand practice, try one candid: Open waiting-hand practice. Look for what is missing, then check each candidate against the whole hand. A hand can have more than one winning tile.
Keep the draw steady in the game and wat: Watch the archer for a moment before releasing. The body moves as you aim, so the best angle may pass by only briefly. Wait for that position instead of trying to correct the aim just as you let go.
Learn Mahjong online with free beginner: Learn Mahjong online with free beginner exercises. Practise chi and pong, put together a winning hand and find the tiles it is waiting for.
Learn to read a Mahjong hand one group a: Start with the tiles you will see in a Mahjong hand: dots, bamboo and characters, plus winds and dragons. Practise picking out pairs, runs of three in one suit and sets of identical tiles. Those groups are the building blocks of the exercises.
Learn to recognise dots, bamboo, charact: Start by recognising the pictures on the tiles. Once you can tell the suits and honors apart, you can try the first exercises.
Learn whose discard you can claim for ch: A normal turn is draw one, discard one. Chow, pung and kong change that sequence, so it helps to follow each move separately.
Level 1 gives you six single-colour offi: Level 1 offers single-colour offices with matching buses ready to go. Later you will meet offices with two colours and buildings marked with a question mark. When the loop has only three spaces left, a mixed office can still help if the first riders it sends can board and open space for the rest.
Level 1 has six single-colour offices an: The six offices use three colours. Every colour has a shuttle available, and there are no mixed or mystery offices. Use the six moves above or pick a different front office.
Lift the top nut from a bolt and put it: Every bolt starts as a small stack of nuts. You can lift the top nut and move it to a bolt with room, provided that bolt is empty or the nut on top is the same colour. The level is solved when each occupied bolt holds nuts of a single colour.
Look around the edge for a gate a block: Take a quick look around the edge when the board opens. Find a gate that a matching block can already reach. Removing that block gives others somewhere to slide, which is often faster than moving several pieces to make space in the middle.
Look at which part of the screen the tre: Each treatment starts with a prompt showing what to use and where it goes. Look there before moving a tool. Sometimes the instruction is to tap, and sometimes you need to keep dragging or swipe across the marked area.
Look for a familiar beginning or ending: Start by looking for a likely first letter or a familiar pair. Say the word to yourself before you swipe, then follow the letters in order. The route your finger takes is the spelling you submit.
Look for all three copies before tapping: Before taking the first tile, look for its other two copies. If the third is buried, check which tile covers it. The safest opening often removes a complete set that also uncovers something you already need.
Look for the open route from the hive to: Look at the dog and the hive before you draw. A line across the direct route may still leave a gap at either end. Use the available ground or a wall to close off a route the bees could take around your drawing.
Look past the ramp before accelerating o: The rider can clear a ramp and still crash on landing. Look beyond the takeoff before holding the accelerator. If the next slope drops away, straighten the bike to meet it. If a hazard is just after the ramp, leave time to brake.

Make two anime avatars with their own ha: Make a pair of anime avatars with different outfits, hair and accessories. Match the looks with a shared detail or style each character separately.
Match identical tiles along a clear row: Line up matching tiles in Mahjong Puzzle: Tile Match. Clear straight rows and columns and move other pairs into alignment.
Match identical tiles in this Mahjong Co: Connect identical mahjong tiles around corners in Mahjong Lines. Learn the two-turn rule and open routes through a crowded board.
Match selectable tiles to clear each sto: Look for pairs you can use right away, then check where the pieces you want later are sitting. If one half of a pair is exposed and the other is covered, choose removals that get you closer to the covered piece.
Match three identical tiles at a time in: Clear the board in Master of 3 Tiles by making triples. Use visible sets first and avoid filling the tray with unmatched tiles.
Match three or more bubbles of the same: Pop groups of three or more in Bubble Shooter: Tap & Pop. Learn to reach high clusters, use wall shots and work toward each level's goal.
Merge identical ingredients to make dish: Merge ingredients, fill café orders and restore old rooms in Piece of Cake: Merge & Bake. Start with a dish you can make from the board.
Move each crystal to a cell of its colou: The picture is made of coloured cells, many already occupied by the wrong crystals. Pick up a crystal and move it to a matching cell when one is open. Sometimes the spot you want is occupied, so the storage area gives you somewhere to put the crystal in the meantime.
Move screws between holes to release ove: Free overlapping metal plates in Screw & Pin: Puzzle Levels. Move screws between holes and keep a spare hole for the next pin.
Move the top ball of a flask to an empty: Each flask is a stack. Only the exposed ball can move, so a colour you need may be sitting under two others. Look for a place to put the top ball and check what you would uncover by moving it.
Move the top nut to an empty bolt or a m: Play Nuts Puzzle: Sort By Color. Move top nuts onto matching bolts, use spare space well and work around hidden colours.
Open storybook boards in Mahjong 3 and c: Open storybook boards in Mahjong 3. Clear matching tiles, uncover new pairs and finish the board to collect its stars.
Paint a numbered picture in Numicolor. S: Fill numbered shapes in Numicolor. Use the palette highlight to find each colour area and a hint for the last unpainted spot.
Pick a place from the Town map and give: Pick a place on the map and start with an everyday idea, like making a snack or getting ready to go out. Put the characters where the action starts and move the objects they need within reach.
Pick a word with an uncommon letter or a: Choose a word with a letter that stands out, such as Q or Z, or with two unusual letters together. Find those letters first and read the line on either side. This can be quicker than checking every instance of a common first letter.
Pick an animal and decide what you want: Choose an animal and look at the shape of its hair before picking a tool. Decide which part to change first. Work on that section, then look at the animal as a whole before choosing another tool.
Pick an obstacle and keep it in the same: Start with one obstacle and aim for the same part of it twice. A hit in the middle can send the ragdoll a different way from a glancing blow at the corner. Watch what the figure strikes next after the first impact.
Pick an outfit, shoes and hairstyle in I: Style an idol doll for a livestream or fashion event. Choose clothes, shoes and hair, then check how the whole outfit looks on stage.
Pick the outfit item you want the audien: Start with the outfit piece you want people to notice. Add shoes and hair that work with its shape. Use jewellery or makeup for a small repeated colour so the look holds together when you zoom out.
Pick the size and picture for your jigsa: Choose a picture and decide how many pieces you want to put together. A smaller puzzle lets you recognise most pieces by the picture alone. At a larger size, details like a line of roof tiles or a sudden change in colour start to matter.
Pick two identical tiles in the flat gri: Mahjong Lines lays the tiles out in a flat grid. Select two of the same design and they disappear if you can trace an open route between them. That route can run straight or bend up to twice. The tiles between the ends of the route matter just as much as the pair itself.
Pick what to serve before shopping. Use: Pick what you want to serve before shopping. Check the ingredients for that dish and get those first. Once everything is ready, follow the preparation steps and watch for the next tool or ingredient the game highlights.
Place a lever and a machine where you ca: Start with a lever and one machine. Put them somewhere you can see both as you test the connection. Throw the lever, watch the machine, then reset the scene before making it more complicated.
Place coloured gems in matching mosaic c: Fill a gem mosaic in Jewel Coloring. Use the buffer below the board to free a cell, then return the gems to their colours.
Place coloured hexagon stacks next to on: Sort coloured hexagon stacks in Hexa Master 3D. Place matching colours next to each other and keep a free space for a future merge.
Place one cat in each row, column and co: Solve CatDoku by placing one cat in each row, column and colour region. Use the no-touching rule to rule out nearby squares.
Place robots, props and machines in a ph: Build a physics scene in Ragdoll Robots: Sandbox. Connect a lever to a machine with a wire and test what happens before adding more parts.
Plant the first eggs somewhere you can f: Start with an egg you want to try and plant it somewhere you can find again. Leave a path between eggs so it is easy to walk up to each slime when it hatches.
Play Basket Random against the computer: Play Basket Random solo or with a friend. Learn the W and Up arrow controls and time your jump for a falling ball.
Play chess against the computer or anoth: Play Master Chess against the computer or another player. Learn how to move a piece, respond to check and spot simple threats.
Play Clock Out!, a free bus sorting puzz: Play Clock Out!, a free bus sorting puzzle. Match riders to four shuttle queues, work around the 27-space loop and learn how to recover from a jam.
Play English checkers online. Move diago: Play English checkers online. Learn when a diagonal jump is compulsory and how to make kings or block an opponent's last move.
Play Glass Twist, a free online screw pu: Play Glass Twist, a free glass screw puzzle. Match three screws per box, open the layers in order and learn how to clear a jammed tray.
Play Klondike Solitaire on Treasure Isla: Play Klondike Solitaire on Treasure Island. Build four suit foundations and open face-down cards before committing your next move.
Play Ragdoll Soccer solo or with a secon: Play Ragdoll Soccer solo or with a second player on the same device. Approach the ball from the side you want to defend and time the hit.
Play ragdoll sword duels in Epic Sword B: Fight ragdoll sword duels in Epic Sword Battle. Judge your reach, wait for an opening and move out of range after a swing.
Pour from the top of a milk tea bottle i: The bottles hold layered drinks. You can pour the top colour into a bottle with room when its top colour matches or it is empty. Pick moves based on the layer you will uncover, especially when two colours block each other.
Pour matching layers of milk tea into bo: Sort the drinks in Milk Tea Sorting by pouring matching colours into bottles. Learn when to use the spare bottle and how to free it again.
Prepare the hair, then work on one part: Start by preparing the hair, then decide which sections will stay long and which you want to shorten. Work on one section at a time and step back to see the whole outline before cutting again.
Pull yarn from knitted shapes and pack i: Unravel a knitted shape in Yarn Fever! Match strands to open boxes and keep temporary slots free for colours you cannot pack yet.
Race a dirt bike through Moto X3M. Accel: Play Moto X3M online. Learn the bike controls, land safely after ramps and choose where a flip can improve your time.
Read question-mark offices before openin: Decide whether a new building is worth opening before its neighbours.
Read the first waiting passengers and th: A clear road gets a bus out of the lot. Matching passengers are what get it out of the loading area. Move cars and buses in an order that does both jobs before the available spaces fill.
Read the game’s movement and attack prom: When several mobs approach at once, move where you can see them coming. Take on the nearest threat before walking straight into the rest. A step to the side can keep the next enemy in sight while you deal with the first.
Read the level target before swapping ge: Look at the target before swapping. A match in an open area can remove gems without helping you reach the part of the board you need. Scan close to the blocking pieces first and check how a match there would open the grid.
Read the outline of the picture first. A: The outline of a picture can hide the order of its arrows. Start where a tip points out through the outline. After the first piece goes, look at the tracks crossing its old position. That is where the next safe options usually appear.
Read the quest at the top of the board b: On a new board, take a moment to read the quest. The largest group is worth clearing if it gets you closer to that goal or gives you a clean angle to reach it.
Read the task before leaving the room. T: The activity on screen tells you what to do in the house. Read it before walking to another room. Turn the camera to see doors and objects around you and look for the one that matches the task.
Release an office, read the four bus que: Learn how to send a building of workers home.
Restore a farm in Hedgies. Plant crops,: Restore a neglected farm in Hedgies. Grow crops, turn supplies into crafted goods and make time for cooking or fishing as the farm opens up.
Roll the dice and move your checkers int: Play Backgammon and bring your checkers home. Learn how to use dice rolls, protect single checkers and start bearing off.
Rotate a cube and remove pieces in the d: Take apart a cube in Arrow Cube 3D. Rotate across all six faces and remove arrows with a clear path out.
Rotate a wooden model in Tap 3D Wood Blo: Take apart a wooden shape in Tap 3D Wood Block Away. Rotate the model to check each block's full exit path before trying to remove it.
Run a school obstacle course in Escape S: Run a school obstacle course in Escape School Duel. Learn both players' keys and use a double jump to recover or cross a long gap.
Build an arcade in My Arcade Center. Learn how to move, decide where to reinvest and expand as machines bring in earnings.
Search cafés, kitchens and cluttered roo: Search cafés, kitchens and cluttered rooms in Hidden Object: Clues and Mysteries. Pan across each scene and find the objects on your list.
Search the streets and rooms in Hidden O: Find the listed objects in Street Of Secrets. Pan across each location and use outlines and landmarks to spot clues in busy scenes.
See the first six blue screws and the ne: Learn the opening moves for Glass Twist level 2 with real gameplay screenshots. Match box colours, manage temporary slots and avoid common glass puzzle traps.
See what makes a standard Mahjong hand w: Fourteen tiles are only a starting point. To win, they must form the right groups. Start with the usual four sets and a pair.
See when a full 27-space loop can clear: Plan around the 27 waiting places and recognise when a full loop can clear.
Select a palette number to highlight mat: Pick a number and look for the highlighted shapes. Start with the largest area you can see and work inward. The unfilled pieces of that colour become easier to spot once the broad patches are done.
Send buses from the crowded lot to pick: Clear the parking jam in Bus Escape: Clear Jam. Match vehicles to waiting passengers and keep a parking space free for the next bus.
Set up an in-game stunt with ramps, obst: Build a stick figure stunt with vehicles and ramps. Compare setups in Break Stick Completely and see what changes the crash score.
Shape, polish and decorate acrylic nails: Design acrylic nails in a 3D nail salon. Follow the customer's brief from nail shape and polish through to the finishing charms.
Slide blocks through gates of the same c: Slide blocks out through matching gates in ExitBlocks. Clear blockers in the right order before the colour puzzle's timer runs out.
Solve a 9×9 Sudoku with pencil marks. Us: Solve Sudoku with the Notes button. Pencil in possible digits, narrow the candidates and learn how to spot a forced move on the 9×9 grid.
Solve a classic 9×9 Sudoku in your brows: Solve a classic 9×9 Sudoku online. Learn how to use crossing rows, columns and 3×3 boxes to place a digit without guessing.
Sort a Mahjong hand by suit, mark the se: A cluttered hand makes it hard to see what is missing. Arrange the tiles, then look for complete groups and groups needing one more tile.
Sort coloured balls into flasks, one col: Put one colour in each flask in Ball Sort Puzzle. Move exposed balls and use an empty flask to uncover a colour buried underneath.
Sort crystals into empty cells of the sa: Move crystals into matching cells in Jewel Coloring: Crystal Sorting. Use the temporary tray to untangle crossed colours and uncover the picture.
Sort the tiles by suit and put identical: There is no need to memorise every term before looking at a hand. Start with two questions: which tiles are identical, and which numbers form a run? Both will help when you learn claims and winning hands.
Start Glass Garden with six blue screws:: The glass garden gives you several exposed screws at once. A good start is to fill the blue boxes without using the tray, then follow the new box colours as the glass opens up. Here is a practical opening and a way to think through the busier middle of the puzzle.
Start in Beginner if you are learning ti: Beginner covers the tiles and winning shapes. Intermediate lets you work through chi, pong and kong calls and find the tiles you are waiting for. Advanced adds special patterns and a guided hand. Choose the skill you want to practise and use the matching illustrated guide if you need another example.
Start on the part of the arcade you can: Start with the machines you can already manage. Watch where customers spend their time. A busy part of the floor can make a better first investment than a part nobody has reached yet.
Start with an open mosaic cell and bring: Work from a patch with open cells. Place a gem there and check the cell it came from. If the old cell belongs to a different colour, you now have somewhere useful to bring a gem from elsewhere on the board.
Start with the customer's request. Choos: Read the picture or request at the start of the appointment. A set starts with a shape and a polish colour, and those choices do most of the work. Leave the charms until you can see how the base looks across the whole hand.
Start with the smallest region. Cross of: Find a region with few available cells and check which placements are legal.
Summon warriors and heroes in Age of Her: Send warriors and heroes into battle in Age of Heroes. Defend your tower, read the advancing line and build a push against the enemy tower.
Suppose blue is absent from all four sto: If no front bus wants blue, two blue offices use 18 places. Look for a bus that will free places before tapping a third unrelated office. A preview bus can board riders only after the bus in front leaves.
Swap neighbouring candies to make horizo: Match candy in Popping Candies by swapping neighbours. Spend your moves on the level objective and set up matches next to stubborn blockers.
Swap neighbouring gems to make a line of: Swap gems in Diamant: Match 3 Sky Story. Clear obstacles near the level's target and build up a city in the sky.
Swap two neighbours to make a straight l: You need at least three matching candies in a straight line. An obvious swap can still be a poor choice if it clears pieces far from the target. Look at the goal first, then search in the part of the board where a match would make a difference.
Swipe through letters to find every targ: Connect the letters in Word Finder. Try shared beginnings and endings when you have one word left to find in the level.
Take apart pictures made of arrows in Ar: Unpick arrow pictures in Arrows: Escape. Read each arrow's path to the edge and avoid collisions that cost hearts.
Tap an arrow when its lane to the edge i: Play Arrows Out! and untangle crowded arrow boards. Find an open lane, zoom in on tricky gaps and work in from the edges.
Tap neighbouring blocks with the same nu: Tap neighbouring blocks with equal numbers in Block Blast 2048. Set up the next merge before using the pair in front of you.
Tap neighbours with equal values to merg: Look for equal numbers sitting next to each other and tap to merge them. The new block needs to reach another block of the same value before you can merge it again.
Tap Start twisting, then pick an uncover: Tap Start twisting, then a screw with no glass covering it. A screw visible through another plate is still blocked. Match the screw colour to an open box.
Tap to flip the knife through objects in: Flip a knife and slice through Cut It 3D. Time each tap for the next object and leave room to get past the obstacles.
The detective gives you a list for each: A detective takes you from one location to the next. In each scene, a list tells you what to look for. A shelf full of cups or a desk crowded with clocks can hold more than one clue, so give yourself a moment to see where one object ends and the next begins.
The four large shuttles are the ones tak: Look at the four large buses. Each takes three riders of its own colour. A full bus departs and the small bus immediately behind it moves up. Read up to three upcoming buses in each lane from top to bottom. Their animal badges help you tell similar colours apart.
The third matching screw closes a box an: Screws enter a matching open box automatically. Three of the same colour fill it, and the next box arrives. Waiting screws move from the tray whenever a matching box opens.
The tray offers three shapes. Drag them: Block Blast Master is a drag-and-drop block puzzle. The tray offers three shapes at a time. Fit them into the grid as shown and fill a whole row or column to clear it. A piece can finish a row and a column at once if you have prepared both lines.
The usual winning hand has four sets and: A standard winning hand has four sets and a pair. Try laying out what is already complete before deciding what to keep. For example, if 4 and 5 are the only unfinished bamboo tiles and everything else is complete, either 3 or 6 of bamboo can finish that run.
Throw a ragdoll at different obstacles i: Test throws in Ragdoll Crash-Test: Throw and Break! Compare impact angles and see how the ragdoll reacts to different obstacles.
Time your drive with one shot control in: Hit your farthest golf shot in Golf Orbit. Use the one-button timing cue, then compare where your attempts land.
Time your throw when the needle reaches: Throw food farther in OBBY: Throw Food for Pets! Hit the green launch window and time the bounce to bring in a new pet.
Trace an arrow across the cube in the di: Inspect more than the face in front of you. A piece near the middle may run toward a side whose exit you have not seen. Rotate and follow that direction until you can see where the piece needs to go.
Try a single Sprunki character and one p: Place one Sprunki character and an object close enough to interact. Test how they move before filling the space with more props. You can see which object did what when the scene has only a few parts.
Try Klondike if you want to uncover hidd: Try Klondike if you want to turn over hidden cards and build four suit piles. FreeCell shows the whole deal and gives you holding cells to move cards around. Empty holding cells are useful, so move a card back out as soon as it has a better place.
Turn the camera until you can see both t: Turn the camera until both the edge of your platform and the landing are in view. At a corner, stop and face the next jump before you take it. A side view can make an angled landing look closer than it is.
Two checkers on a point protect it from: The dice give you movement distances, but you choose which checkers to move. A single checker on a point can be hit. If moving it leaves another one exposed, compare which point the opponent is more likely to reach on the next roll.
Two matching tiles can clear along a row: A straight gap is what matters here. Two identical tiles in the same row or column can match through empty spaces. If another tile interrupts the line, move it or play a different pair first.
Undo restores the board and all four que: Undo restores the board and all four bus queues to before the last office opened, once per round. Expansion adds nine places, up to 36, and clears the undo history. Keep expansion for a jam if you need it.
Undo takes back one move while you have: Yes, while you have undo uses left. Restart resets the whole layout if you need to rethink the opening.
Unmatched screws go into the tray above: Screws without a matching open box wait in the 5 slots above the board. Check the box colours before taking one; a full tray jams the round after automatic matching.
Use five tile diagrams to recognise two-: A common mistake is missing another tile that also wins. Work through five complete hands rather than relying only on the names of the waits.
Use Notes when a blank could be filled in more than one way. Suppose only 2 and 8 fit a square. Mark both. If an 8 later appears in the same column, you know you can replace those notes with a 2.
Use the list to narrow the search. A sma: The hotel looks cluttered because the objects sit among believable furniture and decorations. Start with the list, then search where an item could fit. Look along the back of a shelf or beside a piece of furniture where the outline could blend in.
Use the music as a cue for a turn, then: Use the beat to remember when a difficult turn comes up, and keep your eyes on the shape of the passage. Two beats can sound alike while the spaces ahead have different widths.
Use the on-screen controls to clear bloc: Use a sword against block-style monsters in Mine Fight! Cut Mob Army! Make space to swing and clear the enemies in each stage.
Use the starting tasks to decide what to: Use the early tasks to decide what to plant. Before using a crop in a recipe or a craft, check whether the next task needs that same crop. It can be useful to keep enough for one more job before committing the rest.
Walk through the house and complete each: Explore the house in Pregnant Mom Simulator Family Life. Follow each activity prompt and use the right controls to interact with objects.
Wash, cut and style hair in Hair Salon. Choose the tools in order and check the shape before adding the finishing touches.
Watch how far each wave makes it across: Your tower needs time for the army to build up. If an opponent's wave reaches your side, spend on the troops you can use to stop it. When your army starts moving forward, use the space it wins to reinforce the push.
Watch the needle as it sweeps into the g: The throw has two moments to watch. Start with the needle in the circle. Let it reach green before you tap. Once the food is in the air, watch its landing area so you can catch the second timing cue.
Watch the sword’s movement in the game b: Stand far enough away to see the opponent's next swing. When their sword moves past you, close the distance if you have room to reach them. Watch your own fighter's movement so you can step out again after the attack.
Watch the timing cue through a full pass: Watch the indicator across a full pass before taking a shot. Pick a fixed mark near the best part of the cue and use it to time the input. Repeat from the same setup to see how predictable the result is.
Watch where the blade is heading before: Each tap changes the knife's motion. Look a little ahead of its current position and decide where you want it to meet the next object. Tapping rapidly makes it harder to tell which flip sent it too high or too low.
Watch where the front zombie in each lan: Watch the first wave before committing all your resources. A lane that already has enough damage can hold for another moment. Use your next placement where the first zombie is closest to getting through.
Watch which side is moving the front lin: Before deploying anything, work out who is moving the line. If your front units are holding, save for something that can help them push. If they are about to collapse, an immediate reinforcement can matter more than an expensive unit arriving too late.
When a box has two screws, check the who: A third matching screw opens the next box and may bring waiting screws out of the tray. Look for a useful match before collecting another colour.
When a shuttle leaves, check its replace: Wait for three matching riders to fill a shuttle, then read the new front colour in that lane. Before opening another office, see if that bus can pick up anyone already on the loop.
When the exposed screws are all the wron: When none of the exposed screws matches, look for an off-colour screw that shifts a whole plate. It is worth taking up a slot if the move uncovers the third screw you need for an open box. A screw that exposes nothing may cost the same slot and leave you no closer to a match.

When you call chow or pung, combine the: Chow and pung claim a tile another player has just discarded. You combine it with tiles from your own hand and show the completed set. That visible group is called an exposed set.
With 1, 2, 4 and 5 characters in hand, a: This follows the turn-sequence guide. That guide explains the actions; this one uses specific tiles to compare the available choices and the hand each leaves behind.
Work out which goal you are defending be: Before charging the ball, look at which goal is behind you. If you hit from the wrong side, you may send the ball toward your own end. Move around it when there is time and make contact in the direction you want it to go.
You are looking only for frogs. Check sh: In this hidden object game, the only things you need to pick out are frogs. Before one is found it can look like a rock or a leaf. Look for two round eyes or a folded rear leg, then follow the lines to see whether they belong to a frog.
You start with two open boxes and 5 temp: You start with 5 temporary slots and two open boxes. Each box takes three screws of its own colour. For example, if the blue box already holds two screws and the tray has a yellow one, look for an exposed blue screw first. Filling that box brings in the next colour. If it is yellow, the screw in the tray packs itself and gives you a slot back.
